records.claim: Masked Majority Function training directly exercises extraction of a majority relation under visual interference, uncertainty and limited exposure time.
records.approved_public_wording: Attention Coach is closely aligned with goals involving signal extraction under visual interference and time pressure.
records.required_caveat: This construct fit does not establish improvement in every form of attention or everyday focus.

records.claim: MFT-M attention-control training has initial randomised evidence of transfer to selected attention-task conditions and verbal-learning acquisition trials.
records.approved_public_wording: Initial controlled research found transfer to selected attention measures and verbal-learning trials.
records.required_caveat: Independent replication, delayed follow-up and workflow outcomes remain needed.

records.claim: Current direct and broader evidence does not establish consistent improvement in sustained everyday focus from MFT-M training.
records.approved_public_wording: Attention Coach is designed to train controlled attention, while everyday focus improvement remains an outcome to test rather than a promised effect.
records.required_caveat: The broader literature is heterogeneous across populations, tasks and outcome measures.

records.claim: The SART provides a task-based index relevant to sustained engagement and response control, but performance also reflects response strategy and speed-accuracy trade-offs.
records.approved_public_wording: G Track uses the SART to estimate engagement stability and response-control performance during a repetitive task.
records.required_caveat: No single SART error score should be interpreted as pure inattention or as identifying the cause of poor performance.

records.claim: Stroop and Flanker tasks have strong experimental construct bases for conflict and selective-attention effects, but conventional difference scores may have limited reliability for individual-difference assessment.
records.approved_public_wording: G Track combines condition-level Stroop and Flanker performance with other indicators rather than relying on one interference difference score.
records.required_caveat: The exact short forms, scoring model and test-retest performance require prospective validation.

records.claim: The Open Matrices Item Bank provides a validated, calibrated source of figural matrix items.
records.approved_public_wording: G Track uses matrix items from the validated Open Matrices Item Bank.
records.required_caveat: The selected G Track form, longitudinal sensitivity and score interpretation require implementation-specific validation; it is not an official IQ test.

records.claim: Complex-span tasks provide an established paradigm for maintaining information while performing an interleaved processing task.
records.approved_public_wording: The G Track complex-span-style task is based on established working-memory methods.
records.required_caveat: The exact G Track symmetry-span-style implementation remains provisional and non-diagnostic.

records.claim: Visual change-detection and binding paradigms provide an established basis for measuring feature and feature-location conjunction memory.
records.approved_public_wording: The G Track binding task is based on established visual working-memory binding paradigms.
records.required_caveat: The exact digital implementation and workflow relevance require separate validation.

records.claim: Working-memory training can produce small improvements on untrained working-memory measures, with larger effects when assessment tasks resemble the training task; current meta-analytic evidence does not support fluid-intelligence improvement.
records.approved_public_wording: Working-memory training can improve some working-memory outcomes, but broader reasoning gains are not established.
records.required_caveat: Task similarity can inflate apparent transfer, and this evidence does not validate the exact WM Coach implementation.

records.claim: Controlled evidence includes findings that updating and binding training do not transfer broadly, so WM Coach workflow and far-transfer benefits remain hypotheses to test.
records.approved_public_wording: WM Coach targets defined relational and binding-memory operations; broader transfer is measured separately and is not guaranteed.
records.required_caveat: Training-task gains should be reported separately from untrained working-memory, reasoning and workflow outcomes.

records.claim: The current paired-task secondary analysis supports an exploratory four-component description of task-active control and a related but non-identical engagement-vigilance dimension.
records.approved_public_wording: G Track provides a provisional behavioural context estimate that becomes more informative across repeated sessions.
records.required_caveat: The profiles are not validated natural kinds, diagnoses, brain states or proven intervention selectors.

records.claim: Computerised cognitive training in ADHD shows short-term working-memory benefits and a small, setting-sensitive inattention effect, but not consistent total-symptom, hyperactivity-impulsivity, laboratory-attention or inhibition benefits.
records.approved_public_wording: IQ Mindware may be relevant to non-clinical attention and working-memory goals associated with ADHD-style difficulties.
records.required_caveat: The apps do not diagnose or treat ADHD, and category-level evidence does not establish efficacy of the exact IQ Mindware protocols.

records.claim: Working-memory training has a small meta-analytic anxiety-reduction signal, but this does not establish Attention Coach or WM Coach as anxiety interventions.
records.approved_public_wording: A non-clinical cognitive route may be relevant when worry competes with focused performance.
records.required_caveat: Do not claim anxiety treatment or symptom reduction from the current apps.
